DISPUTE POLICY Customers must notify the service provider of any disputed invoice within ten business days of receiving the invoice. A dispute should identify the invoice number, the disputed amount, the reason for the dispute, and any supporting documentation. Examples of disputed items may include an incorrect charge, incorrect quantity, incorrect tax amount, duplicate charge, or service that was not received. Each invoice should have a unique invoice number. The invoice date should accurately represent the date on which the invoice was issued. Invoices should clearly identify the goods or services for which the customer is being charged. The total amount should reflect the applicable charges, discounts, taxes, and adjustments. PAYMENT POLICY Invoices must be paid within thirty days from the invoice date unless different payment terms have been agreed in writing. The payment due date is calculated from the invoice date. For example, an invoice dated June 1 is due on July 1. Customers should make payments using one of the payment methods specified by the service provider. REFUND POLICY Customers may request a refund when they have been incorrectly charged, charged for a cancelled service, charged twice, or charged an amount that does not match the agreed invoice. Refund requests should include the invoice number, customer details, reason for the refund, and relevant supporting information. The service provider may review the transaction before approving a refund. Additional documentation may be requested when the reason for the refund cannot be verified using the available billing information. Approved refunds

Approved refunds are normally processed within seven business days after the refund request has been approved. If an invoice was paid using an electronic payment method, the refund will normally be returned using the original payment method. TERMINATION POLICY Either party may terminate the agreement by providing thirty days written notice unless a different termination period has been agreed in writing. Termination notices should clearly identify the agreement being terminated and the intended termination date. Immediate termination may occur if a party materially breaches the agreement and fails to correct the breach within fifteen days after receiving written notice. written notice. A material breach may include a significant failure to perform an important contractual obligation. The party receiving a breach notice should take appropriate corrective action within the specified fifteen-day period. If the breach is corrected within the allowed period, immediate termination on the basis of that breach may not occur. Termination does not remove obligations relating to confidentiality, intellectual property, or payments that became due before termination.
